significance: The principal temple of Cherthala, where the goddess is worshipped in an aniconic form set below ground level and held to be self-manifested. Its Cherthala Pooram is reckoned second among Kerala's poorams and is unusual for an Aarattu performed twice daily; Gandhi addressed a gathering here on 18 January 1937.
story: The saint Vilwamangalam Swamiyar is said to have consecrated the goddess at this spot on his way back from installing the deity at the Padmanabhaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram.
